items.q: Which blood film finding appears earliest in megaloblastic anaemia?
items.exp: Neutrophil hypersegmentation (six or more lobes) precedes anaemia in megaloblastic change and signals impaired DNA synthesis. Macroovalocytes accompany it as deficiency advances.
r: Incorrect. Target cells suggest thalassaemia or liver disease.
Correct. Hypersegmented neutrophils appear earliest.
Incorrect. Spherocytes indicate membrane loss or immune haemolysis.
Incorrect. Schistocytes indicate microangiopathic haemolysis.
items.kp: Six lobes or more means megaloblastic until proven otherwise.

items.q: Loss of vibration and proprioception with extensor plantars in a macrocytic patient indicates what?
o: Subacute combined degeneration from B12 deficiency
items.exp: B12 deficiency degenerates dorsal and lateral cord columns, mixing lost proprioception with upper motor signs. Folate deficiency does not cause this cord syndrome.
r: Incorrect. Folate lack does not injure the cord.
Correct. Combined cord degeneration means B12 deficiency.
Incorrect. Diabetes causes length dependent sensory neuropathy without this pattern.
Incorrect. Motor neurone disease lacks sensory loss and macrocytosis.
items.kp: Cord signs plus macrocytosis equals B12 deficiency. Treat fast.

items.q: Methylmalonic acid is raised in which deficiency?
items.exp: B12 is cofactor for methylmalonyl CoA conversion, so its deficiency raises methylmalonic acid. Folate deficiency raises homocysteine without raising methylmalonic acid, separating the two.
r: Incorrect. Folate deficiency leaves methylmalonic acid normal.
Correct. Raised methylmalonic acid marks B12 deficiency.
Incorrect. Iron deficiency does not affect this pathway.
Incorrect. Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, not this change.
items.kp: Both raise homocysteine; only B12 raises methylmalonic acid.

items.q: Pernicious anaemia results from autoimmune destruction of which cells?
items.exp: Autoimmune gastritis destroys parietal cells, removing acid and intrinsic factor needed for B12 absorption. Intrinsic factor antibody is the specific serological marker.
r: Incorrect. Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, not intrinsic factor.
Correct. Parietal cell loss causes pernicious anaemia.
Incorrect. Enterochromaffin cells secrete serotonin related products.
Incorrect. Paneth cells defend intestinal crypts.
items.kp: Pernicious anaemia is parietal cell autoimmunity.

items.q: Why must B12 be checked before giving folate to a megaloblastic patient?
o: Folate corrects blood counts while B12 cord injury progresses
Folate causes haemolysis in B12 deficiency
Folate invalidates all later tests permanently
items.exp: Folate can normalise blood indices in B12 deficiency while neurological damage advances silently and becomes permanent. Measuring and treating B12 first avoids this masking trap.
r: Incorrect. Folate does not block B12 uptake.
Correct. Folate masks blood signs while cord injury advances.
Incorrect. Haemolysis is not the mechanism of harm.
Incorrect. Tests remain possible, but delay causes damage.
items.kp: Folate without B12 covers the blood and harms the cord.

items.q: Which macrocytosis occurs WITHOUT megaloblastic change or hypersegmentation?
items.exp: Alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism and reticulocytosis enlarge red cells without megaloblastic nuclear changes. Hypersegmentation therefore separates true megaloblastic states.
r: Incorrect. Pernicious anaemia is megaloblastic by definition.
Correct. Alcohol macrocytosis is non megaloblastic.
Incorrect. Methotrexate blocks folate and causes megaloblastic change.
Incorrect. Folate deficiency is megaloblastic.
items.kp: No hypersegmentation means look beyond vitamins.

items.q: Periconception folate supplementation prevents which fetal abnormality?
items.exp: Folate during neural tube closure in the first month prevents spina bifida and anencephaly, so supplementation must start before conception. Later treatment cannot reverse closure failure.
r: Incorrect. Heart block follows maternal anti Ro antibodies.
Correct. Folate prevents neural tube defects.
Incorrect. Clefting has multifactorial causes beyond folate timing.
Incorrect. Chromosomal trisomy is not folate preventable.
items.kp: Folate works before closure, so start before conception.

items.q: Terminal ileal resection most likely causes deficiency of which vitamin?
items.exp: B12 intrinsic factor complex absorbs only in terminal ileum, so resection or Crohn disease there causes B12 deficiency years later as stores deplete.
r: Incorrect. Folate absorbs in jejunum, spared by ileal loss.
Correct. Ileal loss causes B12 deficiency.
Incorrect. Vitamin C absorbs proximally.
Incorrect. Vitamin K issues follow fat malabsorption broadly.
items.kp: Terminal ileum equals B12 absorption. Remember the site.

items.q: Methotrexate induced megaloblastic change is rescued by which agent?
items.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, and folinic acid bypasses the block as reduced folate. This rescue protects marrow and gut during therapy.
r: Incorrect. B12 does not bypass folate blockade.
Correct. Folinic acid rescues antifolate toxicity.
Incorrect. Iron does not correct DNA synthesis failure.
Incorrect. Vitamin C has no rescue role here.
items.kp: Leucovorin rescues methotrexate by bypassing the block.

items.q: Which feature separates B12 deficiency duration from folate deficiency after gastrectomy?
o: B12 stores delay deficiency for years while folate falls in months
items.exp: Hepatic B12 stores sustain years without absorption, while folate stores deplete within months. Post surgical timing therefore hints at which vitamin failed first.
r: Incorrect. B12 onset is delayed by large stores.
Correct. Years for B12, months for folate.
Incorrect. Folate stores are short, not decades.
Incorrect. Neither depletes within days.
items.kp: Months means folate; years means B12.
